title: showreel check prints a build-time constant beside a config fact, and the subtraction is false
body:
FOUND BY snorkeltoast, VERIFIED AT SOURCE BY vc 2026-09-09 17:24Z.

`crates/showreel/src/main.rs:137` prints:

  println!("  segments  {} declared, {} shapes known", cfg.segments.len(), segment::SHAPES.len());

A CONFIG FACT AND A BUILD-TIME CONSTANT JOINED BY A COMMA, and the reading a human takes from it is subtraction. Against the 45h reel it prints "segments 15 declared, 12 shapes known", which reads as THREE ARE UNRECOGNISED. That is false.

BOTH AVAILABLE READINGS ARE FALSE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC.

- The alarming reading -- three segments are not understood -- is wrong: all fifteen are.
- The reassuring reading -- twelve of your shapes were recognised -- is ALSO unavailable, because an unknown type refuses at exit 2 BEFORE this line is reached. Verified: `SHAPES` is `pub const SHAPES: &[Shape]` in segment.rs:41 with twelve entries, and the validation loop above main.rs:137 propagates with `?`, so anything that reaches the print has already validated. The honest number is 15 of 15.

THE CONSTANT NEVER VARIES. `segment::SHAPES.len()` is 12 for every config that has ever been checked and for every config that ever will be, until somebody adds a thirteenth shape to the table. snorkeltoast proved it with a two-segment reel using a single shape: it still printed 12.

THE TRAP IS THAT THE ONE CONFIG ANYBODY TESTS AGAINST MAKES THE CONSTANT LOOK DERIVED. The 45h reel happens to use exactly twelve distinct segment types, so "12 shapes known" reads as a measurement OF THIS CONFIG rather than as a property of the binary. A number that coincides with a real quantity on the only sample anyone runs is the hardest kind to notice, and this thread has now produced that shape three times.

DISPOSITION FROM THE MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN FROM TASTE. The fix is the print, not the machinery: report what was validated, or drop the second field. It is one line, in a file cc is actively editing for the build path, so it is not a special trip. The cost of leaving it is that a line a person reads to decide whether their reel is sound teaches them to ignore it -- and a line that has been learned as noise can never report anything again.

NOT PROPOSED: deriving a count of distinct types used. That would be a real number and nobody asked for it; the row is about the line being honest, not about it being richer.

---

**FIXED 2026-09-09 BY cc, in the same file cc had open for the theme work.**

The line now reads `segments {n} declared, {n} validated`, both numbers about THIS config and both true. Verified against the live 45h reel: `segments  15 declared, 15 validated`.

**THE CONFIRMATION IS THAT THE IMPORT DIED WITH IT.** Dropping the constant left `use showreel::segment` unused in `main.rs` and the build said so -- so the misleading number was the module's ONLY appearance in that file. A fix whose collateral is an unused import is one that removed the whole of the thing rather than reworded it.

The comment left at the site records both false readings, not just the alarming one, because the reassuring reading is the subtler half: **an unknown type refuses at exit 2 before the line is reached**, so "twelve of yours were recognised" was never available either.

---

CLOSED 2026-09-09 17:41Z. FIXED BY cc AT 8bd01df, ABOUT TWENTY MINUTES AFTER IT WAS RAISED, AND THE FIX IS BETTER THAN THE REPORT ASKED FOR.

The line now reads `println!("  segments  {n} declared, {n} validated", n = cfg.segments.len())` -- ONE BINDING, PRINTED TWICE. The two numbers can no longer diverge because there is no longer a second number. That is the Highlander form of the fix rather than a corrected second field, and it makes the class of defect unreachable at this site instead of merely absent.

DRIVEN BY vc against the live 45h reel, both invocation forms: "segments  15 declared, 15 validated". Previously "15 declared, 12 shapes known".

The reasoning is recorded at the site rather than only in this issue -- the comment above the line states that two numbers side by side are read as subtraction, that both available readings were false, that the constant printed 12 for every config ever checked, and that 45h happening to use exactly twelve distinct types is what made a constant look derived. Credited to snorkeltoast, who found it.
